findings.body: When `origin` is `null`, this sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` together with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. Browsers reject that combination per the Fetch/CORS spec, so credentialed clients that omit Origin still fail preflight/response checks. Prefer omitting CORS allow headers (or using a concrete allowlisted origin) when Origin is absent — native apps typically do not need CORS headers at all.

summary:
## Verdict

**Critical security regression** — this PR turns a strict origin allowlist into reflect-any-origin CORS with credentials, which lets any website read credentialed API responses.

## Analysis

`corsHeaders` previously only emitted `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (and credentials) when the request `Origin` was in a fixed allowlist (`https://app.example.com`). The new code always returns:

- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <request Origin or *>`
- `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`

That combination is the classic CORS misconfiguration: a malicious page can trigger a credentialed cross-origin request (cookies / auth headers the browser attaches automatically) and **read the response**, because the browser sees its own origin echoed back as allowed.

The PR rationale (“native mobile clients do not send a fixed origin”) does not justify this. CORS is enforced by browsers/WebViews; native HTTP clients are not subject to it. Missing or non-allowlisted origins should stay denied (empty headers), or legitimate WebView origins should be added to the allowlist.

Secondary issue: when `origin` is `null`, the response is `ACA-Origin: *` together with `ACA-Credentials: true`, which the Fetch spec forbids and browsers reject — so the null-origin path is both insecure in intent and non-functional for credentialed calls.

`Vary: Origin` is fine on its own but does not mitigate the open reflection.

## Recommendation

Restore an explicit allowlist (extend it if mobile WebViews use known origins). Never pair `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` with a reflected or `*` origin outside that list.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: Head `corsHeaders` always echoes the request Origin (or `*`) and sets `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, removing the prior allowlist. That enables any site to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses, matching a critical CORS misconfiguration.
